To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RGD cadherin family members are involved in the metastasis of colorectal cancer and other solid tumors, and their expression is associated with a poor prognosis in patients with colorectal cancer.
RGD cadherin family members, including VE cadherin and CDH17, promote metastasis in cancer by activating a2b1-integrin, and that this activation is critical to cancer progression.
the RGD motifs of CDH17 and of VE-cadherin activate a2b integrin and that this activation is critical in the late steps of liver and lung cancer metastasis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of RGD cadherin and a2b integrin in cancer progression.
the identification of new RGD cadherin family members, and their role as ligands for a2b1 in cancer metastasis.
the role of the a2b1/CDH17/VEcadherin axis in cancer metastasis, and with the development of new agents to block this axis in cancer metastatic progression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
RGD motifs of cadherins are critical for the activation of a2b integrin, a key player in the metastatic process.
RGD cadherin and a2b integrin are key partners in cancer metastasis.
RGD motifs in cadherins are important for cancer progression.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have discovered a new family of cadherin molecules with RGD motifs that bind to the b1 integrin and activate its function.
we have demonstrated that the RGD motifs of VE-cadherin and CDH17, two cadherins expressed at metastatic sites, are critical actors in cancer cell invasion and metastasis.
we have demonstrated that the cadherin family is much more complex than previously thought, that RGD motifs are not restricted to integrin-binding ligands and that they can be found on cadherins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the RGD motif, a well-known ligand for integrins, is also an integrin ligand itself.
the RGD motif is a critical actor in the metastatic cascade.
the RGD cadherin family is a new player in the field of integrin activation in cancer metastasis, and that targeting RGD cadherine could be a novel strategy for the treatment of cancer.
